tagline: A de-esser that finds every S, SH and T in your vocal and lets you set each one's level
description: Put Hush on the vocal and press play: it captures the take and lights up every sharp sound (each S, SH, CH and T) on the waveform, labelled and in its place. Each one gets its own level in the lane below: drag a single harsh S down by 9 dB, leave a soft one alone, or let Amount handle them all, louder ones more. Only what's above Freq is turned down, through a zero-phase split, so the voice underneath never moves. Before you capture, it de-esses live.
highlights: One fader per sound: every S, SH and T the vocal makes is found and drawn where it happens; drag its handle down to lower just that sound, by any amount from 0 to -30 dB
Amount sets them all at once (harsh ones more than soft ones), then you fix the few that need it by hand; ALL S / ALL SH / ALL T select a whole kind, AUTO and BYPASS reset a selection
Click a sound to hear it inside its word; arrow keys step through them; Shift-click or drag a box to move several together; Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes

Clean: Split mode crossfades only the part above Freq to a zero-phase low band, so with no cut the vocal comes out sample-for-sample identical, and with a cut nothing below Freq changes. Wide mode turns the whole sound down

Follows the vocal by itself, like Contour: play the song and Hush picks it up and finds every sharp sound; your levels play live in the mix with no latency, changed or re-recorded parts are picked up as they play, and audio not yet picked up is de-essed live
Listen switch to hear only what is being taken out; optionally PRINT the result to a WAV and drag it onto a track
18 presets for natural, firm, rap, airy pop, breathy R&B, high and low voices, INTERNET GIRL, neo soul and soul, a heavy lisp fix and hand-only editing
Favourites: star the presets you love and browse just those; your stars survive updates
installTips: Put Hush on the vocal's mixer track (after Contour if you use it, before compression and reverb), press play over the part you want to de-ess, then stop: the sounds appear.
Your levels play live in the mix: there is nothing to record or drag out. If you change or re-record the vocal, just play that part: FOLLOW (lit in the top bar) picks the new take up by itself.
Optional, to print it as audio: PRINT, then drag DRAG OUT into the playlist and drop it at bar 1.

In Ableton, work in Arrangement View (Session clips have no fixed place in the song, so the take can't line up with them). To print, drop DRAG OUT on an audio track at 1.1.1 and switch the clip's Warp off.
previewNote: on a synthetic sung phrase with S, SH and T consonants of different loudness, captured and played back through each preset.

items: No record or drag-out step: Hush follows the vocal on the track by itself (FOLLOW in the top bar). Play the song and every S, SH and T appears; your levels play live in the mix; change or re-record a part and it picks the new take up as it plays
PRINT (was BOUNCE) is now optional: only to turn the result into a WAV
INTERNET GIRL presets (the Cape Town punk / hyperpop / trap trio): Distorted Shout and Hyperpop Air
Windows open at a size that fits your screen (about 80 % of a laptop's height) and can be dragged bigger; the size you pick is kept
Smoother windows: the static panels, shadows and grain are drawn once and reused, so meters and lights no longer redraw the whole window (3 to 4 times less drawing)
